text:
Nina P.: Quick design question: when smoothing + outlier-clipping is enabled, we abbreviate y-axis ticks (e.g., '1.2k'). Users on support reported confusion about units and scale. Proposal: expand ticks on hover/focus to show full text and provide an SR-friendly announcement. Sam W.: Agree. Instead of always showing full labels (which clutters), show abbreviated ticks by default and on hover/focus reveal full label inline. For keyboard users, focusable tick elements make sense. Aisha: For screen readers, rely on aria-describedby on the chart to provide context: "Chart updated: smoothing enabled; y-axis units: requests per minute." Also announce when a tick is focused: "Tick: 1,200 requests per minute." Use role="button" on tick elements. Jon M.: Small CSS/JS note: expanding inline could shift layout. Better to expand as an overlay tooltip anchored to the tick so it doesn't reflow. Tooltip must be accessible (aria-live or aria-label) for keyboard and SR users. Nina P.: UX microcopy options for tooltip/announce: - "1,200 requests/min" - "1,200 requests per minute" - "1.2k requests/min (exact: 1,200)" Which is clearest? Aisha: Go with the long form for SR and the compact with exact for visual tooltip: visual -> "1.2k (1,200) rpm"; SR -> "1,200 requests per minute". Keep verbs clear. Sam W.: Implementation sketch: ```html 1.2k
1,200 requests per minute
``` ARIA behavior: when focused, set aria-hidden=false and push a polite aria-live update: "Tick focused: 1,200 requests per minute". Jon M.: Also consider reduced-motion and touch: on touch devices, long-press should show the tooltip. On hover devices show on hover. Nina P.: Accessibility checklist for PR: focusable ticks, tooltip has accessible name, SR gets full unit announcement, aria-live for chart updates (smoothing/clipping + outlier counts), tooltip respects reduced-motion. Aisha: Add a test to ensure aria-live contains both state and unit: e.g., "Chart updated: smoothing enabled; 2 outliers hidden; y-axis unit: requests per minute." That will help debugging support tickets. Sam W.: I'll prototype the overlay tooltip and keyboard interactions. Jon, can you add the test skeleton for the aria-live string? Jon M.: Yep, will add tests and a visual snapshot. ETA EOD. aria-bot: Note: design review scheduled in the weekly UX slot. Please attach the prototype when ready.
